title: Maps, products and equality testing for inverse-image unit presentations
statement: For unit presentations p of T as L(S) and q of T-prime as L(S-prime) [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-pullback-unit-presentation], two maps out of T agree whenever their composites with p.unit agree on all source sections. If L preserves finite limits, the cartesian product of the two units presents the product of T and T-prime as L of the product of S and S-prime. A map a:S to S-prime transports by the presentation isomorphisms to T to T-prime, and this transported map sends p.unit(x) to q.unit(a(x)).

source.place: Tag 00YV and Modules on Sites Tag 03D2: preservation of algebraic operations by finite-product inverse image; the testing criterion is adjunction injectivity.

proof.text: Conjugate the two maps by p.iso.inv and apply injectivity of the set-sheaf adjunction hom equivalence. Its value is precomposition by the unit, so the presentation equation and the assumed equalities on sections prove equality.

For products use the product of the presentation isomorphisms followed by the inverse finite-product comparison of L. After applying the forward comparison, the two components of the unit equation are naturality of the adjunction unit at the two projections and the two input presentation equations.

Define the transported map by i_p followed by L(a) followed by i_q inverse. Substitute the presentation equation for p, use naturality of the unit at a, then the inverse of the presentation equation for q.
